Arizona Cardinals.longComment: Carter was designated for return from injured reserve 16 days ago, so Arizona will need to make a decision on him next week. Carter has yet to play in a game this season after being injured back in August.

Gaines will miss his sixth straight game in Week 12 due to an ankle injury. With Gaines being on the sidelines again, 2025 sixth-rounder Hayden Conner will project as the Cardinals' top option off the bench on the interior of the offensive line Sunday.

The tight end returned from injured reserve two weeks ago and has two grabs for 18 yards on three targets in two games since suffering a knee injury. Long is now dealing with an ankle issue. Teagan Quitoriano would see an uptick in snaps behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins if Long is unable to play.

Love will miss a fourth consecutive game Sunday but will then be eligible to come off injured reserve ahead of Week 13 against the Eagles. LaFleur previously said Love will be reevaluated Monday once eligible to return, and the coach added Friday that he expects to know more Wednesday once the Cardinals return to practice. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are still the leading in-house backfield options in the meantime.

Beck has yet to resume practicing and will miss a second consecutive game Sunday due to back spasms, paving the way for Josh Johnson to start against Washington. LaFleur added that a Week 13 return against the Eagles is in play for Beck, who made his first regular-season NFL start in a 34-6 Week 10 loss to the Rams. Beck's practice participation level leading up to that game will provide an indication regarding his potential availability, and LaFleur added that the team will know more about Beck's status "early in the week," per Weinfuss.

Atlanta Falcons.longComment: Bergeron has started all 10 games this season and played all 631 offensive snaps. It's unclear when he suffered the injury, but Kyle Hinton and Andrew Vorhees are options to replace Bergeron at left guard against Minnesota.

Hellams played a season-high 62 defensive snaps against the Chiefs in Week 10 and logged 11 tackles (seven solo) in the loss. He apparently suffered an injury in the contest and will miss his first game of the season. Hellams' main contributions have come on special teams.

Bowman was unable to participate in practice all week due to a hamstring injury that will sideline the second-year defensive back for the fourth time in the Falcons' last five games. Sydney Brown will operate in an elevated role in the secondary in the absence of Bowman, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Lions on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Branch will join Jahan Dotson (hamstring) on the sidelines in Week 12. Drake London, Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair are Atlanta's available options at wide receiver, while Zaccheaus and Khalil Herbert are the top candidates to handle punt and kickoff returns in Branch's absence. Branch's next opportunity to suit up will be Sunday, Dec. 6, against Detroit.

Dotson hasn't practiced all week, so it wouldn't be surprising if he's ultimately ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings once the Falcons release game designations Friday. Zachariah Branch (hamstring) also remained sidelined at Friday's practice, so Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair may be Atlanta's only healthy and available wide receivers behind Drake London against Minnesota.

Baltimore Ravens.longComment: Ioane popped up on Thursday's report as a limited practice participant due to a hand injury. He did not practice Friday, so the rookie first-rounder will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines, which leaves Ryan Neuzil and Emery Jones as the top options to start at right guard. Baltimore is on a bye for Week 13, so Ioane's next chance to suit up is Week 14 against Tampa Bay on Sunday, Dec. 13.

Madubuike is set to miss a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Chargers. With the Ravens on a bye for Week 13, the seventh-year defensive lineman's next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 13. Broderick Washington and Aeneas Peebles are both in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in Madubuike's absence.

Hawkins' absence will extend to six games due to a knee injury that he sustained in a practice session during Week 7 prep. The Ravens are on a bye for Week 13, so perhaps the extra rest will be enough for Hawkins to be cleared to return for Week 14 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 13.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: Benford will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a groin injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Jets. Maxwell Hairston should see a bump in defensive snaps at outside cornerback in the absence of Benford, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: Franks popped up on the Panthers' injury report with a wrist injury Thursday, and now there's a cloud over his status for Week 12. He may end up taking an injury designation into game day if he's not able to upgrade to full participation at practice Saturday.

Okereke has been sidelined for the Panthers' last three games because of a foot injury, and his availability for Week 12 is now in doubt. Unless he's able to return to practice Saturday, it's not likely he'll be able to suit up Monday against the Buccaneers.

Evans took a step in the right direction by practicing to some extent Friday after being listed as non-participant on Thursday's estimate. He'll have one more chance to reach full participation Saturday ahead of Monday's game against the Buccaneers. Evans had his best game of 2026 in the Week 11 win over Baltimore, catching all five of his targets for 44 yards and his first touchdown of the season.

Tremble was limited again Friday after being listed a limited participant on Thursday's practice estimate. He has one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation Saturday, which could help Tremble avoid an injury designation for Monday's game against the Buccaneers.

Brooks has shed any practice limitations, but he'll still need to be added back to the active roster to play Monday in Tampa Bay. Even if Brooks gets the green light to suit up and is activated by the Panthers, he'll likely have to settle for a change-of-pace role behind Chuba Hubbard against Tampa Bay's excellent run defense.

Waller was among four Panthers tight ends to have a capped session Friday, the others being Tommy Tremble (knee), Mitchell Evans (Achilles) and Feleipe Franks (wrist). Waller was able to play through his knee injury this past Sunday against the Ravens, when he handled a 46 percent snap share en route to three catches (on three targets) for 42 yards.

Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported earlier Friday that McMillan was in a helmet and pads, and although he ditched them while stretching he put them back on shortly afterward. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will include McMillan's activity level, if any, after he was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate due to a sore foot.

Incoom was placed on injured reserve in late October due to a calf injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Eagles. Regardless of his practice participation over the next three days, the Panthers would have to activate Incoom from injured reserve in order for him to be available for Monday's NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers.

Christensen has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury all year, but he was not activated from IR within 21 days of returning to practice, so he'll now miss the rest of the season. The veteran guard will now have to look forward to hopefully returning at some point in 2027.

Horn is currently considered day-to-day, but head coach Dave Canales wants to ensure Horn is in a great head space before returning. The 2021 first-round pick has been sidelined since late September, while Chau Smith-Wade has handled slot-cornerback duties in his absence. The Panthers will still have to officially activate Horn off injured reserve before he's eligible to return.

Chicago Bears.longComment: Schefter reported earlier that the Bears planned to place Loveland on injured reserve due to the knee injury the TE sustained in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions, which would rule Loveland out for at least four games. Chicago wants to gather more information before a determination is made on Loveland's status, and the door is still open for a shorter absence, though it would be surprising at this point if he's able to play Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Jaguars.

Williams seemingly went for a precautionary X-ray after Week 12 action due to a "weird fall" that occurred during Thursday's contest in which he engineered two TD drives in the final 8:20 of the fourth quarter to eke out a four-point victory. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and recorded three carries for 15 yards. With plenty of time to recover before the Bears' next game Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Jaguars, Williams has a decent chance to avoid practice restrictions next week.

The cornerback didn't practice at all this week and will miss a second straight game after he was injured in Week 9 against the Bucs. Clark Phillips handled third cornerback duties in last Sunday's win over the Saints.

Johnson injured his ankle in Sunday's win over the Saints, and with the quick turnaround for Week 12, he won't be available against the Lions. The Bears will roll with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai as their only healthy backs for Thursday's game.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: Davis was a full participant at practice all week, but he's still on injured reserve with his hamstring injury as of Friday. It looks like he might have to wait one more week to return to game action. If so, 2024 fifth-rounder Josh Newton will likely continue to get increased reps at cornerback against a pass-first Saints offense.

Risner will sit out his second consecutive contest in Week 12 because of a knee injury he sustained back in Week 10 versus the Steelers. In his stead, 2025 fifth-rounder Jalen Rivers figures to make another start at right guard.

Iosivas had his 21-day window to return from IR opened Nov. 12, so the Bengals are running out of time to add him back to the active roster before he would need to miss the remainder of the season. If Iosivas isn't activated ahead of Sunday's game, expect such a move to transpire early the following week before the Bengals travel to Cleveland. Dohnte Meyers has been filling in as Cincinnati's No. 3 WR during Iosivas' ongoing absence.

Higgins wasn't on the Bengals' Week 12 injury report until Friday, but after missing the team's final practice, the wideout's status is now worth tracking ahead of Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. While a late-week downgrade in practice participation like this can't be ignored, Ben Baby of ESPN.com notes that "Higgins just woke up with some soreness" Friday and that the team gave the WR "the day to work through it." More importantly, Baby indicates that the issue isn't a concern in terms of Higgins' availability versus New Orleans.

Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: The rookie third-rounder didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee injury, but he drew the questionable tag after ending Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. Zak Zinter would likely start at right guard in the event that Barber is not cleared to play Sunday.

The veteran edge rusher was injured in Week 10 against the Texans but was able to return to the contest. The Week 11 bye wasn't enough time for Barnett to get right to play against Las Vegas. Sam Williams and Jamree Kromah will see elevated snaps along the defensive line.

Sanders was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he would need to be added to the active roster with an official transaction prior to Sunday's game to have a chance to play. Even if Sanders gets the green light, he's unlikely to see much action on offense, with Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Jaleel McLaughlin all healthy in Cleveland's backfield.

With Boston now on track to log a trio of 'DNP' listings this week, his status for Sunday night's game against the Raiders is cloudy. Friday's final injury report will reveal whether the Browns' starting WR has any chance to play versus Las Vegas or is ruled out ahead of Week 12 action.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Williams tweaked his back late in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game and did not return, finishing with four tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks. The veteran defensive lineman's practice reps during Week 13 prep will ultimately determine what his status will be against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

Moore strung together three consecutive full practices during Week 12 prep, but he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Thanksgiving Day. The rookie fourth-rounder has yet to make his 2026 regular-season debut due to a hip injury that he picked up in training camp.

Locke entered the league's concussion protocol following the Cowboys' Week 9 win over the Colts. He hasn't progressed enough in his recovery to return for Thanksgiving Day and will thus miss a third consecutive game. Locke's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

Mingo's absence for Thanksgiving Day will be his third missed game in a row due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Colts. His absence means KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown will continue to operate in rotational roles on offense behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy. Mingo's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

Bland was placed on injured reserve Sunday after suffering an ankle injury during the Week 10 loss to the 49ers, but the injury is not expected to be season-ending. The earliest Bland will be eligible to make his return is the Week 16 matchup versus Jacksonville, and Ameer Speed and Cobie Durant should continue to see increased playing time in his absence.

Denver Broncos.longComment: Jones had previously been ruled out for Friday's matchup versus the Steelers but will now be forced to miss at least four games before he's eligible to return. In his absence, Tyler Onyedim should be in line for increased playing time.

Lohner was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 12 prep. However, the second-year pro is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, so his next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. Lohner is in the final stages of his recovery from a procedure on his foot in June.

Tuesday was Denver's first practice, and given Elliss's absence, he's highly unlikely to participate in any of the Broncos' next two sessions ahead of Black Friday. The third-year linebacker is recovering from an ankle injury that landed him on IR in late October. Assuming he doesn't play in Week 12, Elliss's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Detroit Lions.longComment: Wonnum was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday, but that didn't end up being enough for him to suit up Thursday. He leads the Lions with 7.0 sacks this season, so the veteran defensive end's absence is a big deal for Detroit. Tyler Lacy, Ahmed Hassanein, Eric O'Neill and Anthony Lucas could all be involved in trying to fill the void left by Wonnum's absence Thursday.

Clark dealt with a hamstring issue during Week 12 prep and is going to miss his first game of the campaign as a result. He's been a starter at safety for the Lions all season and played every defensive snap in three of Detroit's past four games. Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch will start at safety Thursday, with Andre Cisco working in reserve.

Gill-Howard suffered a season-ending knee injury during the Lions' Week 11 win over the Buccaneers. The rookie sixth-rounder will finish his first NFL campaign with 11 tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, across 10 regular-season games.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: Prior to leaving, the linebacker recorded four tackles (two solo). Dani Dennis-Sutton and Brenton Cox will see an uptick in snaps off the edge for Green Bay.

The wideout hasn't cleared concussion checks and will miss the remainder of the Week 12 contest after he was injured at the end of the second quarter when Watson took a hit to the head from Kamren Kinchens. Look for J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton to see increased snaps alongside Matthew Golden and Savion Williams with Watson sidelined.

Franklin drew the questionable tag for Wednesday's game following three consecutive limited practices. However, the veteran linebacker will end up missing a fifth consecutive game due to a hairline fracture in his shin that he suffered during a practice session in late October, so Ty'Ron Hopper will continue to operate in an elevated role on defense. Franklin's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Coming out of the Packers' Week 11 bye, head coach Matt LaFleur told Matt Schneidman of The Athletic on Saturday that he didn't expect Jacobs to play in Week 12, but he also gave the running back a "chance to prove" he can. Jacobs then was listed as limited on practice reports Sunday through Tuesday and tagged as questionable ahead of Wednesday's game. Such activity wasn't enough for Jacobs to get the all clear to suit up, meaning Green Bay's backfield will be manned by Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks for a second consecutive contest.

LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

Houston Texans.longComment: Rutledge was not cleared to practice due to a neck injury that he sustained in the Texans' Week 11 win over the Colts. He won't be available Sunday, so Febechi Nwaiwu will likely draw the start at left guard. Rutledge's next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Steelers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Hunter is set to miss a third consecutive game due to a hamstring injury. In his absence, Jadeveon Clowney and Dominique Robinson will continue to operate in elevated roles on the Texans' defensive front opposite NFL sack leader Will Anderson. Hunter's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Steelers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

The tight end logged a trio of DNPs this week and will miss a third straight contest. With Jordan remaining sidelined, Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau, Marlin Klein and Cade Stover will be the healthy options at the position for Houston. Jordan has two catches for 12 yards on two targets across five contests this season.

Boutte's absence will coincide with the return of Marvin Harrison (hamstring) from a two-game absence. Harrison will join Nico Collins, Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson while Boutte sits out due to an hip injury the latter sustained in last Thursday's win over the Colts, which subsequently prevented Boutte from practicing in any capacity during Week 12 prep. Boutte's next chance to take the field will be Sunday, Dec. 6, at Pittsburgh.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: Tillery will miss a third consecutive game due to a calf injury, so Tim Smith and Kevin Givens will both continue to operate in slightly elevated roles on the interior defensive line behind Grover Stewart and Adetomiwa Adebawore. The Colts are on a bye for Week 13, so Tillery's next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Eagles on Sunday, Dec. 13.
Travis will miss a third straight game, so Matt Goncalves should make another start at right tackle for the Colts.

The cornerback was designated for return from injured reserve earlier in the week and was a full participant all three practice days. Taylor-Britt appears to have a good chance at being activated and playing Sunday. He hasn't played since Week 7 against the Vikings.

Ogletree sat out practice Friday after logging a full session Thursday, casting doubt back onto his availability for Week 12. If he can't play Sunday, it would likely mean increased snaps at tight end for veteran Pharaoh Brown.

Mallory is set to miss a fourth consecutive game due to a hamstring injury. The Colts are on bye for Week 13, so his next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Eagles on Sunday, Dec. 13. Drew Ogletree (knee) is listed as questionable after stringing together a DNP-FP-DNP practice log, and if he cannot play Sunday, then Pharaoh Brown would serve as the Colts' TE2 behind Tyler Warren.

Ward failed to practice in any capacity during Week 12 prep, and the veteran defensive back will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a knee injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Dolphins. He'll have additional time to rest thanks to the Week 13 bye, and Ward will aim to return for Week 14 against the Eagles on Sunday, Dec. 13. Johnathan Edwards, Kapena Gushiken and Kenneth Harris are all candidates to start opposite Sauce Gardner at outside cornerback for Sunday's game.

DJ Giddens is set to inherit change-of-pace duties behind Jonathan Taylor in McGowan's absence. McGowan, who injured his hamstring in the Week 11 loss to the Texans, will have a bye to heal before possibly returning against the Eagles in Week 14.

Curry was placed on the Colts' injured reserve Tuesday, and head coach Shane Steichen informed reporters Wednesday that the rookie sixth-rounder's wrist injury was severe enough for him to require season-ending surgery. Curry will end his first NFL campaign with 26 tackles (14 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two fumble recoveries across 11 regular-season games. His absence means Carl Lawson, Jaylahn Tuimoloau and George Gumbs are all in line for more rotational snaps at defensive end.

Additionally, Pierce acknowledged that playing in Week 1 was a bit lofty, per Bowen, with the WR saying Wednesday that he was still managing some pain at that stage. In any case, Pierce indicated that he's confident that his current recovery plan will lead to a full return to health. When that will be remains to be seen, but the 2022 second-rounder is still on IR ahead of Week 12, with the Colts presumably not planning to rush him back given the team's 3-8 record in a campaign that's been marked by the team moving several key players ahead of the trade deadline.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: The Jaguars' center logged three limited practices this week but could miss a second straight contest after he was initially injured in the Week 10 win over Tennessee. Jonah Monheim started at center last Sunday.

Mekari got in three limited practices this week but will sit out after having his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the week. He's yet to play this season but appears to be knocking on the door of his season debut. Ezra Cleveland has been manning right guard for Jacksonville.

Green has been a full practice participant since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He's not quite ready to return, but with his 21-day window set to close, he would need to be activated from IR during Week 13 prep, otherwise he would be sidelined for the rest of the season. His next opportunity to play is Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Bears.

If Tuten's absence Friday is confirmed by the team's injury report, that would mark a third consecutive 'DNP' for Jacksonville's starting running back. Coach Liam Coen intimated earlier Friday that Tuten's participation level Friday will factor into his potential availability for Sunday's game against the Titans, so he appears more likely than not to sit out Sunday based on this latest development. If Tuten is ruled out, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead a backfield that also includes LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.

Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game in the league to wide receivers. Additional details regarding Washington's injury should emerge before the Jaguars travel to Chicago in Week 13.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: Smith was injured in the fourth quarter of Week 12 action, but the Chiefs never announced the reason for him hitting the sideline until Reid spoke to the media afterward. If the severity of Smith's issue is enough to require an absence or more time off, Hunter Nourzad is the likely candidate to man right guard for Kansas City.

Royals left the game in the third quarter and was ruled out not long afterward due to an ankle injury. The severity of the sprain will determine if Royals is in danger of missing any time. If that comes to pass for Royals, Andrew Armstrong likely will be on track for a few more offensive snaps behind Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, Xavier Worthy and Cyrus Allen.

Despite logging full participation sessions in Week 12 prep, Norman-Lott will not suit up for Thursday night's contest. The Chiefs activated the defensive tackle from the reserve/PUP list Nov. 18, but he is not quite ready to return to the field.
Moore will miss his third consecutive game with an ankle injury. Joshua Ezeudu will once again be called upon to start at right tackle for the Chiefs' offense.

VanSumeren didn't practice Tuesday due to a sprained knee that will now keep him out for at least the next four weeks, according to Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site. In six regular-season games in 2026, the fourth-year pro played a majority of his reps on special teams, with just six of 104 total snaps coming on offense.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Keenan was unable to practice during Week 12 prep due to a knee injury he sustained against the Broncos in Week 11, and his next chance to play is Week 14 against the Chargers on Sunday, Dec. 13. The Raiders will enter the weekend with only two healthy defensive lineman on the 53-man roster in Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi.

Powers-Johnson was injured in Friday's practice, and coach Klint Kubiak suggested it could be a serious injury, according to Sam Warren of The Athletic. He hasn't logged an offensive snap since Week 5 after opening the season as the Raiders' starting right guard. Trey Zuhn has been manning the position.

The defensive lineman sustained a concussion last Sunday against the Broncos and will miss at least one contest while he works through the protocol. With Tim Keenan (knee) also out against Cleveland and JJ Pegues (elbow) questionable, the Raiders may be especially thin up front Sunday night.

Hemingway missed the final two practices of Week 12 prep due to what was classified as a stinger, and the second-year defensive tackle will end up missing his second consecutive game. He'll join Adam Butler (concussion) and Tim Keenan (knee) on the sidelines Sunday, and that leaves Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi as the only healthy defensive lineman on the Raiders' active roster heading into the weekend. With the Raiders on a bye for Week 13, Hemingway's next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Chargers on Sunday, Dec. 13.

Per Sam Warren of The Athletic, Bowers didn't practice Friday after being limited the previous two days. It's unclear if the star TE's 'DNP' to close the week was maintenance or setback related, but the Raiders' late kickoff presents an issue for those considering Bowers in Week 12 fantasy lineups. As one of the marquee names carrying a 'questionable' tag into the weekend, look for added context regarding his status to arrive no later than Saturday night or Sunday morning via the usual notable NFL insiders.

Johnson was a full participant in Wednesday's practice in what was his first on-field action since being placed on injured reserve in late October due to a neck injury. His ability to practice in full is an encouraging sign, but Johnson would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: Williamson was injured in last Sunday's loss to the Jets and logged a pair of limited practices Thursday and Friday following Wednesday's absence. He's yet to play a single defensive snap this season while seeing 129 snaps on special teams.

An ankle injury prevented Tuipulotu from practicing all week, yet the Chargers have kept the door open for the fourth-year edge rusher to suit up for Sunday's contest. Akheem Mesidor (ankle) is listed as doubtful, which leaves Khalil Mack, Caleb Murphy and Bud Dupree as the three healthy edge rushers on the Chargers' 53-man roster heading into the weekend.

Thompson has not played since Week 2 against the Raiders due to a hamstring injury, and it looks like that trend will continue after the rookie fourth-rounder missed all three practices during Week 12 prep. Assuming he doesn't play Sunday, Thompson's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Still did not practice at all during the week after sitting out the Chargers' contest versus the Jets in Week 11 with an ankle injury, but there's apparently still a chance he'll be able to play in Week 12. Otherwise, Isas Waxter might be in line to see an increased snap count at cornerback Sunday.

Mesidor was not able to practice at all during the week because of an ankle injury he sustained in Week 11 versus the Jets, and it looks like he might be trending towards missing his first game of the season in Week 12. If he can't go Sunday, it could mean an uptick in reps on the edge for Caleb Murphy.

Henley will spend a second straight game on the sidelines due to a knee injury in Week 12. In his absence, veteran Troy Dye could get a start at linebacker next to fellow veteran Del'Shawn Phillips on Sunday.

At 1-9, the Chargers have zero incentive to rush Herbert back to the field at this stage. His next chance to see game action thus is slated to arrive Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Buccaneers. In Herbet's absence this weekend, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network relays that DJ Uiagalelei is slated to start at QB for the Chargers, with Jake Browning available to back him up.

Njoku was held out of practice both Wednesday and Thursday due to a shoulder injury that he sustained during the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. He was cleared to return to practice in a limited capacity Friday, which was enough for the veteran tight end to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's contest. Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will maintain expanded roles on offense in the event that Njoku doesn't play, and Patrick Herbert would be a candidate for elevation from the practice squad to give the Chargers more depth at tight end. That said, the Chargers' offensive potential figures to be limited in Week 12 in the absence of Justin Herbert (concussion), with DJ Uiagalelei set to make his first career start.

Mitchell tweaked his knee during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets in Week 11. The injury prevented the fourth-year pro from practicing all week, and his absence for Sunday's contest means Kimani Vidal should operate in an expanded role in the backfield behind RB1 Omarion Hampton. Mitchell's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

It's not clear when Leonard was injured, as he logged a season-high 70 percent defensive snap share against the Jets last Sunday. Regardless, he's now required to miss at least four games while on IR. Avery Smith and Isas Waxter may get more opportunities in the secondary during Leonard's absence.

Tomlinson likely sustained his knee injury in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The defensive tackle will likely need to return to practice by Friday's session for a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: The 29-year-old offensive lineman made his first career start against Green Bay but was injured in the second half after playing 56 of 75 offensive snaps. Justin Dedich came in to replace Murray at left guard.

Allen was injured in the second quarter of Wednesday's win over the Packers. The Rams are still evaluating the extent of Allen's injury, but Rapoport mentions that high-ankle sprains are typically accompanied by recovery timelines of 4-to-6 weeks, so Allen is looking exceedingly unlikely to be available for the Rams' next game next Thursday against the Chiefs.

Higbee and Davis Allen (ankle) were both injured during Wednesday's win over the Packers. Allen likely is facing a multi-week absence due to a high-ankle sprain, but Higbee still has a chance to avoid missing additional action. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare are the only healthy TE options remaining the Rams' active roster.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: He'll miss a second straight game, also Jack Browning should get the nod at punter for Miami. He'll likely be busy Sunday.

Wayne will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a quadriceps injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Broncos on Sunday, Dec. 6. Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert will continue to operate in slightly expanded roles on offense in Wayne's absence.

Brents did not participate in any of the three Week 12 practices while recovering from neck and shoulder injuries that he sustained in Week 11 against the Bills. Darrell Baker will likely start opposite Jason Marshall at outside cornerback in the absence of Brents, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Broncos on Sunday, Dec. 6.
Harrison suffered a hamstring injury in Week 1 that landed him on injured reserve. The fact the Dolphins opted to open his practice window after nine weeks suggests Harrison may be nearing a return.

That said, per Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com, Hafley added that the Dolphins will evaluate the QB's status again depending on how he feels at the end of his minimum required stay on IR. For now, Willis is out for at least three more games, with Kyle McCord currently filling in as 1-9 Miami's starting signal-caller.

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: The Vikings' left tackle has been playing at less than 100 percent for most of this month and aggravated the issue last Sunday night against the 49ers. Ryan Van Demark replaced Darrisaw at left tackle against San Francisco and figures to draw the Week 12 start.

Smith ended Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a thigh injury. In the event that he cannot play Sunday, Theo Jackson would likely start opposite Josh Metellus at safety. Smith has 21 tackles (11 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and five pass defenses (including two interceptions) across 10 games this season.

Per Emily Leiker of The Minnesota Star Tribune, Rodgers sat out practice again Friday due to his quad injury, and he'll now miss his second straight game in Week 12. In his absence, rookie fifth-rounder Charles Demmings figures to see an uptick in snaps on the boundary.

Addison thus will miss a third straight contest due to a thumb injury that required surgery. In Addison's continued absence, the Vikings will lean on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, Myles Price and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver. Addison's next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 6, versus the Panthers.

New England Patriots.longComment: Rouse missed the Patriots' last game before their bye in Week 11 due to a concussion, but after logging a full practice Friday, it looks like there's a chance he could return in Week 12. If he doesn't, Ben Brown could end up being the Patriots' unquestioned top option off the bench on the interior of the offensive line Sunday.

Barmore first appeared on the Patriots' Week 12 injury report Friday as a DNP, which indicates that the knee issue is a new one for the sixth-year defensive lineman. A late addition to the injury report typically isn't a good sign, but Barmore's official availability may not be known until the Patriots announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff. DaQuan Jones and Joshua Farmer would both be in line for more snaps on defense if Barmore doesn't play.

Gilliam returned from injured reserve in Week 10 against the Lions and is now coming off the bye week, but he's still dealing with the knee issue. The fullback has touched the ball two times on offense this season, logging 71 snaps and another 56 on special teams.

Despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 11 bye, Davis was unable to participate in any of the Week 12 practices due to a knee injury and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. Charles Woods will likely start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback Sunday in the absence of Davis, whose next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Bills on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Since the Patriots designated Doubs for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he logged limited listings on injury reports. However, head coach Mike Vrabel told Evan Lazar of the team's official site Friday that Doubs is unlikely to play in Week 12, which now has been confirmed. Doubs will turn his sights to a Week 13 matchup with the Bills on Sunday, Dec. 6.

With Brown unavailable following the Patriots' Week 11 bye, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are in line to handle the team's WR duties in Tommy DeVito's first start of 2026. Meanwhile, Romeo Doubs (shoulder) isn't likely to be activated from IR this weekend, so it looks like the earliest either of New England's top two wideouts could be available is Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Bills.

The move opens Vera-Tucker's 21-day practice window. The oft-injured offensive lineman went down in the Patriots' Week 6 win over the Jets. Greg Van Roten started New England's last game at left guard.

Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: The offensive lineman was injured in Week 10 against the Panthers and was initially expected to miss several weeks. He missed last Sunday's loss to the Bears but appears to have a chance to return following three limited practices. Richards has seen action at both left and right tackle this season.

After missing the previous two games, Fuaga appears to have a chance to return Sunday following a trio of limited practices. Mason Murphy started last Sunday's game against the Bears at right tackle in place of Fuaga.

Fant would be in line to operate as the top TE for the Saints if he gets the green light to suit up against the team for which he played last season. The 29-year-old Fant has scored either three or four touchdowns in six of his eight NFL regular seasons, including three apiece in 2025 with Cincinnati and so far in 2026 with New Orleans. Rookie third-round pick Oscar Delp is the next tight end up if Fant joins Johnson on the sidelines.

Johnson suffered a hamstring injury this past Sunday at Chicago, and he then was listed as a DNP on the Saints' first two Week 12 practice reports, despite head coach Kellen Moore calling the tight end "day-to-day" Thursday, according to Terrell. With Johnson missing his first game of the campaign and Noah Fant (calf) questionable for Sunday's matchup, Oscar Delp is the sole healthy player at the position on the active roster.

New York Giants.longComment: Harris was battling an illness that prevented him practicing during Week 12 prep, and he's not progressed enough in his recovery to play in Sunday's contest. Darius Alexander and CJ Okoye are both in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in the absence of Harris, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the 49ers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Newsome is expected to undergo surgery for a sprained ankle that he sustained in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. Now that he's on IR, Newsome will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Lions on Monday, Dec. 28. Paulson Adebo is expected to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside cornerback in Newsome's absence.

New York Jets.longComment: The veteran defensive lineman was designated for return from injured reserve last week and will look to make his return after logging a trio of full practices this week. Onyemata hasn't played since Week 2.

The veteran defensive lineman has started all 11 games this season, recording 43 tackles (16 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a fumble recovery on 55 percent of the defensive snaps. Jack Heflin would be next up for increased snaps alongside Jowon Briggs and Darrell Jackson if Phillips is unable to play. David Onyemata (abdomen) could also be activated from injured reserve.

The defensive tackle remains on injured reserve after having his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, but he's been fully participating in practice and appears to have a decent chance of being activated Saturday and playing Sunday. Sweat hasn't played since Week 7.

Cooper will miss a second consecutive game Sunday, bringing him up to six total absences as a result of ankle injuries during his rookie campaign. Adonai Mitchell is set to start on the outside opposite Garrett Wilson, with Isaiah Williams manning the slot, though another elevation for practice-squad WR Sterling Shepard could be on the table after Shepard scored twice in the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Cooper's next chance to play will be a Week 14 home game against the Broncos following the Jets' Week 13 bye. Glenn said the timing of the bye played into the decision to keep Cooper out Sunday, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com, which suggests Cooper has a decent chance to return after the bye.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: Smith put together a career stat line during the Eagles' Thanksgiving Day win, with the veteran wide receiver hauling in 11 of 14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns. He was in and out of the game after landing hard on his tailbone on one of his targets in the fourth quarter and was in noticeable pain when on the field. Smith will have additional time to rest courtesy of the Thursday game, but his status over the coming days will be worth monitoring ahead of the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Goedert injured his right shoulder during the first half of Thursday's game and was not cleared to return. He'll undergo further tests to determine the severity of the injury, but the veteran tight end is certainly in jeopardy of not being available for the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6. Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers would all be in line for larger roles on offense if Goedert were to miss time.
Hall exited the game in the second half, casting doubt on his availability for the remainder of the contest. Ty Robinson could see an uptick in playing time if Hall ends up being unable to return.
Epps is done for the day after suffering a foot injury in the third quarter. In his absence, Kenny Moore has taken over at safety.

This marks Barkley's second diagnosed stinger of the campaign, but on the previous occasion in Week 2 against the Titans, he was able to check back in to the contest. The Eagles may opt to exercise caution with Barkley, however, because he tended to a neck issue on a short week following this past Sunday's win against the Steelers.

DeJean was shaken up on the Eagles' first defensive drive of the first quarter and was taken to the locker room, where medical staff diagnosed the third-year defensive back with a concussion. Michael Carter should see more defensive snaps in the secondary in the absence of DeJean, who will now work through the league's protocol in an effort to be available for Week 13 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

After his trade to the Bengals fell through two weeks ago, Ebiketie is now dealing with an injury that will sideline him for at least one contest. Jalyx Hunt and A.J. Epenesa should soak up extra snaps off the edge for the Eagles.

The cornerback was injured in last Sunday's win over the Steelers. With Jones set to miss Thanksgiving Day against Dallas, Riq Woolen and Kelee Ringo are likely to see increased snaps opposite Quinyon Mitchell.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Echols recorded one assisted tackle before leaving the game due to a quad injury that is severe enough for him to not return to Friday's contest. His absence means the Steelers will have less depth both on special teams and in the secondary the rest of the way.

Sawyer tweaked his knee on the final play of the first quarter, and medical staff have determined that the second-year edge rusher's injury is severe enough for him to not return to Friday's contest. With Sawyer done for the day and Alex Highsmith (ankle) inactive, more defensive snaps are available for Nick Herbig and KJ Henry.

Holcomb will sit out Friday's game after popping up on Thursday's injury report with a heel injury. His next chance to suit up will come Dec. 6 against the Texans. Carson Bruener and Jacoby Windmon could get more run as rotational inside linebackers in Holcomb's absence.

Dunker managed to return to practice for the first time since suffering a knee injury in September but will have to wait at least another week before making his return. The rookie sixth-round pick should provide additional depth at guard once healthy.

Highsmith was held out of practice all week due to an ankle injury that he picked up during the Steelers' 19-16 loss to the Eagles this past Sunday, when he logged 2.0 sacks and forced a fumble before his exit. Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer are the top candidates to start opposite T.J. Watt at the edge rusher position in the absence of Highsmith, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Texans on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Skowronek has been working through a calf issue since mid-October, and he appeared to aggravate the injury during the Steelers' Week 11 loss to the Eagles. Now that he's on injured reserve, Skowronek will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 27. Max Hurleman was signed off the practice squad to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: Pleasants was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and ended Week 12 prep with back-to-back full practices. He would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Saturday's NFC West showdown.

Greenlaw was limited at practice all week after sitting out the 49ers' contest versus the Vikings with a neck injury, and now his availability for Week 12 seems like a coin-flip proposition. If he is sidelined again Sunday, Garret Wallow could start in his place at linebacker against a run-first Seattle offense.

Warkins was held out of practice all week due to a groin injury, and the second-year wide receiver will end up missing his third game of the season and first since Week 2 against the Dolphins. Keenan Allen, Jacob Cowing and Demarcus Robinson are all candidates for more offensive snaps Sunday in the absence of Watkins, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Evans didn't practice Wednesday before he was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report as he continues to deal with the right Achilles tendinitis that forced him out of a Week 6 matchup with the Commanders. He returned to action this past Sunday versus the Vikings in Mexico City and gathered in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown on a 43 percent snap share. Evans' status will be clarified about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

Purdy wasn't able to practice during Week 12 prep due to an ankle injury, which will sideline him for the first time this season. In place of Purdy, Mac Jones will earn the spot start Sunday, while the former's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 6, at the Giants. Shanahan added that surgery isn't on the table for Purdy and he's optimistic the QB will be OK to return in Week 13, according to Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com.

McKivitz was diagnosed with a fractured and dislocated ankle that he sustained in the 49ers' Week 11 win over the Vikings. He's expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, and Vederian Lowe is expected to take over as the starter at right tackle in McKivitz's absence.

Okuayinonu suffered a broken foot in practice ahead of Week 1 and required surgery. He appears to be making progress and could return at some point before the end of the regular season. The 28-year-old appeared in 15 regular-season games last season, and made 12 starts and recorded 23 tackles (16 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.

Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: The defensive tackle was injured in the Seahawks' previous contest against the Raiders in Week 10 and will now miss his first game of the season. Reed has 20 tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, on 48 percent of the defensive snaps as a rotational lineman. Rylie Mills and Mike Morris should see more action up front.

Nelson underwent a minor procedure on his knee in early November and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. He's had additional time to rest thanks to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, and Macdonald relayed Wednesday that the team is "hopeful" that Nelson will be cleared to return for Week 13 against the Cowboys on Monday, Dec. 7. Greg Zabel will likely start at left guard in Nelson's absence.

Per John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Wednesday that Lucas is not a candidate for injured reserve but is expected to miss "days to weeks" due to an ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 10 against the Raiders. Josh Jones, Bobby Hart and Chase Lundt are all candidates to start at right tackle for as long as Lucas is sidelined.

Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: Morrison has been a DNP for each of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 11 against the Lions. He would likely need to log at least a limited practice Saturday to have a realistic shot at suiting up for Monday's NFC South showdown against the Panthers.

Winfield has been listed as a DNP for each of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Bears. He did not play against Detroit in Week 11, so he would likely have to log at least a limited practice Saturday to have a realistic chance of suiting up Monday against Carolina.

Johnson wasn't listed on Thursday's practice report, so the illness is a recent development for the second-year wide receiver. His participation level, if any, in Saturday's practice will provide clarity on his status heading into Monday's game against the Panthers.

McMillan hasn't played since Week 3 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, but since he was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he was listed as full with knee and calf issues on Thursday's estimated injury report before Friday's downgrade in activity. Ultimately, Saturday's practice report will determine McMillan's chances to return to action Monday against the Panthers.

Rozeboom has been on injured reserve for the Buccaneers' last four games while recovering from a finger injury that he sustained in late October. Tampa Bay's first practice of Week 12 prep is Thursday, so Rozeboom's participation over those three sessions will determine whether he's recovered enough to be activated from IR ahead of Monday's game against the Panthers.

Simmons played 17 defensive snaps in Sunday's loss but did not appear in the box score. The defensive tackle has now entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact football activities.

Tennessee Titans.longComment: Burgess injured his knee against the Cowboys in Week 11, which prevented him from participating in any of the Titans' Week 12 practice sessions. His absence means that Tennessee will have one less contributor on special teams and less depth at safety behind Tony Adams and Kevin Winston for Sunday's AFC South tilt. Burgess's next chance to play is Week 13 against the Commanders on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Flott picked up a neck injury during the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys in Week 11. He was not cleared to practice during Week 12 prep, and in his absence, Micah Robinson figures to start opposite Joshua Williams for Sunday's AFC South showdown. Flott's next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Commanders on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Robertson will end up missing a second consecutive game due to an ankle injury that he sustained during the final practice of Week 11 prep, and his absence means Quan Martin will once again operate in an elevated role in the Commanders' secondary. Robertson's next chance to play is Week 13 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.
